summary.one_liner: A top-style terminal TUI that monitors every running Claude Code session, showing process stats, busy/idle state, context size, model, git branch, and sub-process/port info.
summary.what_it_does: Shows a live table of all running Claude Code sessions with PID, memory, CPU, uptime, busy/idle state, context size, model, host app, project, git branch, and last prompt. A sub-agent and sub-process tree lists each session's live sub-agents and child processes, including open and orphaned TCP ports. The TUI supports keyboard navigation, a per-session detail view, filtering, and sorting, and it can print a single frame (--once or when piped) or a JSON snapshot (--json). An opt-in notifier rings the terminal bell and sends a desktop notification (OSC 9) when a busy session finishes and waits for input. Users can send SIGTERM to a runaway session (x) or free orphaned ports held by a session (f), each with confirmation. A history dashboard (h) shows past sessions, per-day token usage, and breakdowns by model, tool/MCP, and project. The README says it reads only ~/.claude and the process table and writes only its own preferences and usage cache under ~/.claude/cctop/.
use_cases: monitor multiple Claude Code sessions at once
check which Claude session is waiting for input
find and stop a runaway Claude Code process
free dev server ports left behind by a session
review Claude Code token usage history
track context size and model per session
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | sh  (install script; the README's URL is missing from the text, so the exact URL is not shown)
stack: TypeScript/JavaScript (single Bun program, no npm packages)
notable: Zero-dependency single Bun program; a standalone self-contained binary is also distributed
Notifications via terminal bell and OSC 9 desktop alerts, plus a 'Which session rang?' indicator that remembers the last session to ding
Read-only design: reads ~/.claude and the process table and spawns no processes
Built-in self-updater (cctop upgrade) that verifies checksums and swaps the binary atomically
caveats: Usage-limit display is opt-in and requires adding a cctop --capture-usage line to the Claude Code status-line script
The binary's self-update (cctop upgrade) is the only command that fetches from the network and replaces itself
Desktop notifications depend on the terminal supporting OSC 9 (README lists iTerm2, Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm, Windows Terminal)
